notes.text: Passports and the JR Kansai-Hiroshima Area Pass (day 2 of 5). Out: Sakura 741, Shin-Osaka 06:25. Back: Nozomi 58, Hiroshima 19:06. Both are on the pass, with 8 seats reserved together.
The day before: check Kakiya (it closes on random days) and the Dreamination lighting dates.
Spa World turns away anyone with tattoos, and it's USJ rope drop tomorrow, so it's one hour of baths and out by 23:30.

stops.summary: Sakura 741 at 06:25: the pass pays for the dawn bullet train west. Seats together, breakfast, sleep.
stops.story: Today the JR Kansai-Hiroshima Area Pass earns its money: Osaka to Hiroshima and back on the Shinkansen, plus the Miyajima ferry, on the one pass. You leave Osaka in the dark and roll into Hiroshima at 07:57.
how: Reserve 8 seats in the same car on Sakura 741 when you exchange the pass.
Leave Shin-Osaka at 06:25, arrive Hiroshima at 07:57. Eat an ekiben or konbini breakfast on board.
At Hiroshima, take the 08:21 JR Sanyo local to Miyajimaguchi (08:49), then the 08:59 JR ferry.
tips: Running early? Mizuho 601 at 06:00 reaches Hiroshima at 07:25, and the pass covers it too.
Skip the 08:11 local. It leaves only 14 min after you arrive, which is too tight for 8 people.
Dec 23 is year-end travel season, so reserve as soon as you have the pass.
stops.booking: Reserve 8 seats together when exchanging the pass
wishes: Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days
Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.summary: Spring high tide at 09:29 and you land just before it: the giant torii is standing in the sea.
stops.story: Itsukushima Shrine is built out over the water on stilts, and its huge vermilion torii stands in the bay. Today you get a spring tide with high water at 09:29, so the gate rises straight out of the sea instead of out of the mud. The cold winter air off the water keeps it sharp, and the deer don't care about any of it.
how: The 08:59 JR ferry from Miyajimaguchi lands at 09:09 (on the pass), just before high water.
Walk the shoreline to the shrine and pay ¥300 to walk the corridors over the water.
Take the group shot of the torii from the shore while the tide is in.
tips: The torii is in the water roughly 07:30–11:30 today, so don't dawdle on the island.
Take the JR ferry. It's the one the pass covers.
Don't hold food near the deer.
wishes: Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days

stops.summary: Hiroshima oysters straight off the grill, hot momiji cakes and a cold beer on the island's main street.
stops.story: December is oyster season, and Miyajima's shopping street is full of grills smoking with Hiroshima oysters. Kakiya, the Michelin-listed oyster specialist, does nothing but oysters, and does them properly. Finish with momiji manjū, maple-leaf cakes still warm from the machine.
how: Hit Kakiya first. There are no reservations, so just walk in and order the oyster set.
Graze the street stalls for more grilled oysters and fresh momiji manjū.
Take the 12:37 JR ferry back, then the JR Sanyo line to Nishi-Hiroshima and the Hiroden tram to Dobashi.
tips: Kakiya opens 10:00–18:00 but closes on random days, so check the day before. The street stalls are the fallback.
The tram isn't JR, so pay it separately.
wishes: Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days

stops.summary: The museum that stops every group conversation. Give it the full time.
stops.story: The Peace Memorial Museum shows what happened on 6 August 1945 through ordinary things: clothes, a tricycle, a melted lunchbox. It's not a fun stop and it isn't meant to be, but it's the one everyone ends up talking about years later. Afterwards, the Cenotaph and the Flame of Peace line up across the park.
how: Buy WEB tickets ahead (¥200), because same-day tickets can take a while.
Walk through the permanent exhibits, then out to the Cenotaph and the Flame of Peace.
Walk north across the park to the Dome, 8 min.
tips: Open 07:30–18:00. Only the 16:30–18:00 slots need advance booking, and you'll be there well before then.
Keep your voices down inside.
wishes: Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days

stops.summary: The ruined dome left standing as it was. Ten quiet minutes on the riverbank.
stops.story: The Atomic Bomb Dome is the shell of the building that survived almost directly below the blast, left exactly as it was. Seeing it from the river as the winter light goes is the quiet moment between the museum and the evening.
how: View it from the riverbank opposite. It's outside only, and free.
Walk east along Hondōri to Yagenbori for dinner, 14 min.
tips: Send two people ahead to the okonomiyaki queue from here.
wishes: Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days

stops.summary: Hiroshima okonomiyaki done right: layered on the griddle and crunchy with fried noodles.
stops.story: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki isn't mixed. It's built in layers: batter, a pile of cabbage, pork, noodles fried crisp, egg, sauce. Hassho in Yagenbori is on Tabelog's Top 100 list for it, and you eat it straight off the teppan with a little spatula.
how: It opens at 16:00 and there are no reservations. The plan gets you there at 16:40, so send two people ahead from the Dome to hold a place in the queue.
Expect to sit as two tables of four.
Eat from the teppan with the spatula, not a plate.
tips: Wednesday is fine: it closes Mondays and the 1st/3rd Tuesday.
Fallback: Okonomimura in Shintenchi, a building full of okonomiyaki counters.
Peace Boulevard and Dreamination are a 12-minute walk away.
wishes: Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days

stops.summary: A quick walk through the winter light sculptures on Peace Boulevard, then taxis to the 19:06 Nozomi.
stops.story: Every winter Hiroshima lines Peace Boulevard with light sculptures for Dreamination. You'll walk through for a few minutes on a full stomach, it'll be cold, and then you make the train.
how: Walk straight down Peace Boulevard through the lights.
Leave on time and take 2 taxis to the Shinkansen entrance at Hiroshima Station, 12 min.
Board Nozomi 58, Hiroshima 19:06 → Shin-Osaka 20:31, on the pass.
tips: Check the lighting dates and hours before you go. We have no research record for this stop, only the plan's dates.
Take taxis, not the tram. The tram only reaches the station at 19:01, too tight for Nozomi 58 at 19:06.
Miss it? Nozomi 60 leaves at 19:21 and reaches Shin-Osaka at 20:46.
stops.hours: Check the lighting dates and hours before you go
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Second dinner: deep-fried skewers and highballs under Tsūtenkaku's neon.
stops.story: Shinsekai is Osaka at its loudest: neon, the Tsūtenkaku tower and kushikatsu, which is anything on a stick, breaded and deep-fried. Daruma is the famous name, and its Dōbutsuen-mae branch has 50 seats and takes groups.
how: Take the Midōsuji line from Shin-Osaka at 20:57, reaching Dōbutsuen-mae at 21:15, and walk in.
Order the whole round as soon as you sit down, because last order is 22:00.
Dip once in the shared sauce, and never again after a bite.
tips: The no-double-dipping rule is serious. Use the cabbage to scoop extra sauce.
Tsūtenkaku is a 2-minute walk away.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: Ten minutes under Tsūtenkaku and Shinsekai's old Shōwa neon: the loudest photo backdrop in Osaka.
stops.story: Shinsekai was built to be Osaka's 'new world' and never got the update: giant puffer-fish lanterns, flashing signs and the Tsūtenkaku tower lit up overhead. At this hour the tower deck is closed, so don't bother going up. The street is the show.
how: Walk 2 min from Daruma to the foot of Tsūtenkaku.
Group photo under the tower with the neon behind you.
Walk on to Spa World, 5 min.
tips: The deck is closed by now, so photos only.
It's free and it's on your way to the baths.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: A theme park of hot baths, one floor Asian and one European. One hour, then the last good train home.
stops.story: Spa World is an onsen theme park in Shinsekai, with whole floors of baths themed on Asia and Europe. After a 05:25 start, a bullet train both ways and two dinners, an hour in hot water is what you need.
how: Pay at entry. The official weekday price is ¥2,000.
Pick your floor and soak for the hour.
Out by 23:30 and take the JR Loop line from Shin-Imamiya at 23:47 to Nishikujō at 23:57 (on the pass).
tips: Stay past midnight and the late-night surcharge kicks in: +¥1,300 and ¥150 tax.
Anyone with a tattoo gets turned away. Check before you queue.
A taxi straight to Kujō takes 14 min if the train plan falls apart.
stops.hours: Open around the clock; entry reception paused 8:45–10:00
wishes: A 24-hour onsen night (Thermae-yu in Kabukichō or Spa World in Shinsekai)
